note: Cards for the method, foundations, research, reasoning and interpretation lessons written in the second pass. One fact per card; every card is planted by exactly one lesson.

cardTypes.term: Defined term or Latin maxim. Irreducible pair.
cardTypes.rule: A black-letter rule or a single element of one.
cardTypes.ratio: The principle a case stands for.
cardTypes.source: Where a rule comes from — statute, section, or authority.
cardTypes.trigger: A fact cue that should make you think of a doctrine.

cards.front: What makes a fact 'material' in a case brief?
cards.back: A fact the decision turned on — one whose change might change the result.

cards.front: Why is a headnote never citable?
cards.back: It is written by an editor and is not part of the judgment.

cards.front: What single test separates ratio from obiter?
cards.back: Necessity: would the result stand without the proposition?
cards.note: Length and emphasis are not evidence of ratio.

cards.front: A judgment says the court 'heard no argument and expresses no view' on a point. What follows?
cards.back: That point is obiter and undecided; the case is no authority on it.

cards.front: What is the characteristic failure mode of an IRAC answer?
cards.back: A long Rule section and a thin Application — recall proved, reasoning not.

cards.front: A problem question gives an oddly specific date or sum. What does that signal?
cards.back: It does legal work. An unused specific is usually a missed issue.

cards.front: How is writing time allocated across questions?
cards.back: In proportion to the marks. Overrunning costs more elsewhere than it earns here.

cards.front: What is the civil standard of proof?
cards.back: The balance of probabilities — more likely than not.

cards.front: Who has the constitutional discretion to institute or discontinue a prosecution in Malaysia?
cards.back: The Public Prosecutor, under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.

cards.front: Does an acquittal prevent a civil claim on the same facts?
cards.back: No. The acquittal means the case was not proved beyond reasonable doubt; the civil standard is lower.

cards.front: Which words belong to criminal proceedings and which to civil?
cards.back: Criminal: prosecution, accused, charge, conviction, sentence. Civil: plaintiff, defendant, claim, liability, judgment.

cards.front: What do square brackets around the year in a citation mean?
cards.back: The year is needed to locate the volume — [2010] 2 MLJ 1 is volume 2 of the 2010 MLJ.

cards.front: What do MLJ, CLJ and AMR stand for?
cards.back: Malayan Law Journal, Current Law Journal, All Malaysia Reports.

cards.front: What can a citation never tell you?
cards.back: Whether the case is still good law. That needs a citator, and there is no free Malaysian one.

cards.front: What makes a note of a statutory provision complete?
cards.back: The section, plus which version of the text you read and the date you read it.

cards.front: What makes a difference between two cases a genuine distinction?
cards.back: The earlier court's reasoning must depend on the fact that differs.

cards.front: What may a High Court judge do with a Federal Court decision he thinks is wrong?
cards.back: Distinguish it if the facts allow; otherwise follow it. He cannot decline to follow it.

cards.front: Why are English contract authorities used with care in Malaysia?
cards.back: Contract is codified in the Contracts Act 1950, so the starting point is the Act's words.

cards.front: What does it mean to 'confine a case to its facts'?
cards.back: To read the earlier decision as narrowly as its result allows — legitimate, but a signal of discomfort.

cards.front: Which provision directs a purposive construction of Malaysian statutes?
cards.back: Section 17A of the Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967.

cards.front: When does the purposive approach become relevant?
cards.back: Once the words are capable of more than one reading. It chooses between available constructions; it does not create one.

cards.front: Ejusdem generis — what does it do?
cards.back: General words following a list of specifics are read as confined to the same class.

cards.front: What weight does a marginal note carry?
cards.back: It indicates arrangement. It is not enacted text and cannot control a clear provision.

cards.front: How is an ouster clause construed?
cards.back: Narrowly. Courts start from a presumption against the ouster of their jurisdiction and require clear words.
